evidence.paraphrase: Poirot describes a systematic method of remote investigation through daily reports and instructions.
evidence.quote: You should know my methods by now. All I ask is that you should report to me fully every day, and follow implicitly any instructions I may wire you.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator conducts a careful physical examination of the crime scene and photographs it.
evidence.quote: I examined everything with painstaking care and took a couple of pictures of the room with my little camera, which I had brought with me. I also examined the ground outside the window

evidence.paraphrase: Forensic examination of the bullet establishes the type of weapon used.
evidence.quote: The bullet had been extracted and was proved to have been fired from a revolver identical in size to the one held by the police.

evidence.paraphrase: Poirot proposes a methodical, ordered analysis of the facts to reach the solution.
evidence.quote: let us examine the facts methodically and in order.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts fictional detective stories with the sparse evidence he finds in reality.
evidence.quote: In detective-novels, clues abound, but here I could find nothing that struck me as out of the ordinary except a large bloodstain on the carpet

evidence.paraphrase: An editorial note directly addresses the reader, inviting them to solve the mystery.
evidence.quote: It is suggested that the reader pause in his perusal of the story at this point, make his own solution of the mystery\u2014and then see how close he comes to that of the author

evidence.paraphrase: Havering appears distressed and agitated when seeking help.
evidence.quote: His face, however, was haggard, and he was evidently laboring under great agitation.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator and Japp react with astonishment to Poirot's instruction to arrest the housekeeper.
evidence.quote: Dumfounded, I took the wire to Japp. He swore softly under his breath.

evidence.paraphrase: Poirot uses deductive reasoning about likely behavior to identify a flaw in the criminals' plan.
evidence.quote: A man who has committed a murder with a revolver which he found on the spot would fling it away at once; he would not carry it up to London with him.
